ingredients.name: Paracetamol
ingredients.renal_notes: No reduction usually needed; caution in severe hepatic impairment or chronic alcoholism (max 2000mg/day).
ingredients.notes: Hepatotoxicity risk when cumulative daily intake exceeds 4000mg in adults.

ingredients.name: Ibuprofen
ingredients.renal_notes: Avoid in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30). Increases risk of acute renal failure and fluid retention.
ingredients.notes: GI ulceration, cardiovascular thrombotic events risk with prolonged high dose.

ingredients.name: Aceclofenac
ingredients.renal_notes: Avoid if eGFR < 30. Use lowest effective dose in mild-to-moderate impairment.
ingredients.notes: Widely prescribed in India for osteoarthritis and musculoskeletal pain. Not recommended in pediatrics.

ingredients.name: Diclofenac
ingredients.renal_notes: Contraindicated in severe renal failure. Monitor renal function closely.
ingredients.notes: High risk of GI bleeding and cardiovascular events.

ingredients.name: Mefenamic Acid
ingredients.renal_notes: Avoid in significant renal impairment.
ingredients.notes: Frequently used for dysmenorrhea and spasmodic colic.

ingredients.name: Dicyclomine
ingredients.renal_notes: Use caution in renal dysfunction.
ingredients.notes: Contraindicated in infants < 6 months due to respiratory collapse risk.

ingredients.name: Amoxicillin
ingredients.renal_notes: Reduce dose or extend interval if eGFR < 30 mL/min (max 500mg every 12h).
ingredients.notes: Watch for hypersensitivity/penicillin allergy.

ingredients.name: Clavulanic Acid
ingredients.renal_notes: Adjust with amoxicillin dosing.
ingredients.notes: Prevents bacterial degradation of amoxicillin; causes diarrhea in high doses.

ingredients.name: Pantoprazole
ingredients.renal_notes: No renal adjustment required.
ingredients.notes: Reduces gastric acid. Take 30-60 mins before meals (BBF).

ingredients.name: Domperidone
ingredients.renal_notes: Reduce frequency if eGFR < 30 mL/min.
ingredients.notes: Risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias, especially in elderly or with other QT-prolonging drugs.

ingredients.name: Metformin
ingredients.renal_notes: eGFR 45-59: max 1000mg/day. eGFR 30-44: max 500-1000mg/day. eGFR < 30: CONTRAINDICATED due to high risk of fatal lactic acidosis.
ingredients.notes: First-line Type 2 diabetes agent. Monitor renal panel regularly.

ingredients.name: Glimepiride
ingredients.renal_notes: High risk of prolonged severe hypoglycemia in renal impairment; use conservative dosing or switch to DPP4i.
ingredients.notes: Stimulates insulin release from pancreatic beta cells.

ingredients.name: Telmisartan
ingredients.renal_notes: Risk of hyperkalemia and acute decline in GFR. Contraindicated in bilateral renal artery stenosis.
ingredients.notes: Black box warning: contraindicated in pregnancy (fetal toxicity).

ingredients.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
ingredients.renal_notes: Ineffective if eGFR < 30 mL/min; use loop diuretics (furosemide) instead.
ingredients.notes: Monitors serum sodium, potassium and uric acid.

ingredients.name: Amlodipine
ingredients.renal_notes: No renal adjustment required.
ingredients.notes: Commonly causes peripheral ankle edema.

ingredients.name: Aspirin
ingredients.renal_notes: Avoid high doses in CKD; increases risk of worsening renal perfusion.
ingredients.notes: CONTRAINDICATED in children/adolescents with viral infection due to Reye's syndrome.

ingredients.name: Clopidogrel
ingredients.renal_notes: No dosage adjustment needed.
ingredients.notes: Prodrug requiring CYP2C19 activation. Caution with omeprazole.

ingredients.name: Atorvastatin
ingredients.renal_notes: No dose adjustment required for renal insufficiency.
ingredients.notes: Strictly contraindicated in pregnancy. Risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis.

ingredients.name: Montelukast
ingredients.renal_notes: No adjustment required.
ingredients.notes: Neuropsychiatric adverse events black box warning.

ingredients.name: Levocetirizine
ingredients.renal_notes: eGFR 30-49: 2.5mg every 24h. eGFR 10-29: 2.5mg every 48h. eGFR < 10: Contraindicated.
ingredients.notes: Less sedating than cetirizine.

ingredients.name: Ciprofloxacin
ingredients.notes: Tendon rupture and QT prolongation warnings. Avoid taking with divalent cations (Calcium, Iron, Antacids).

ingredients.name: Azithromycin
ingredients.renal_notes: Use caution in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 10).
ingredients.notes: Risk of QT interval prolongation, torsades de pointes.

ingredients.name: Calcium Carbonate
ingredients.renal_notes: Monitor calcium-phosphate product in CKD patients to prevent vascular calcification.
ingredients.notes: Chelates fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines, and levothyroxine.

ingredients.name: Vitamin D3
ingredients.renal_notes: May require active vitamin D (calcitriol) in severe CKD.
ingredients.notes: Strengths often given in IU. 1 mcg = 40 IU.

ingredients.name: Serratiopeptidase
ingredients.renal_notes: No renal adjustment known.
ingredients.notes: Anti-inflammatory and antiedemic enzyme widely combined in Indian NSAID formulations.

ingredients.name: Tramadol
ingredients.renal_notes: eGFR < 30: Increase dosing interval to 12h, max 200mg/day.
ingredients.notes: Risk of seizures, serotonin syndrome with SSRIs/SNRIs, respiratory depression.

ingredients.name: Tinidazole
ingredients.renal_notes: Supplemental dose after hemodialysis.
ingredients.notes: Severe disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol. Metallic taste.

ingredients.name: Ofloxacin
ingredients.notes: Chelation with antacids and mineral supplements.

ingredients.name: Ornidazole
ingredients.renal_notes: Use caution in end-stage renal disease.
ingredients.notes: Commonly paired with fluoroquinolones for gastroenteritis in India.

ingredients.name: Sildenafil
ingredients.renal_notes: Start with 25mg in severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30).
ingredients.notes: CONTRAINDICATED with nitrates due to profound fatal hypotension.

ingredients.name: Nitroglycerin
ingredients.renal_notes: Use with caution.
ingredients.notes: Concomitant use with PDE-5 inhibitors is absolutely contraindicated.

ingredients.name: Warfarin
ingredients.renal_notes: Increased risk of bleeding in CKD; requires frequent INR monitoring.
ingredients.notes: Extreme bleeding interaction with NSAIDs, antiplatelets, and several antibiotics.

ingredients.name: Omeprazole
ingredients.renal_notes: No renal dose adjustment needed.
ingredients.notes: Potent CYP2C19 inhibitor; significantly attenuates clopidogrel antiplatelet activation.

ingredients.name: Ramipril
ingredients.renal_notes: Initial dose 1.25mg if eGFR < 40. Contraindicated in bilateral renal artery stenosis.
ingredients.notes: Risk of hyperkalemia, angioedema, persistent dry cough. Do not combine with ARBs.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Omeprazole strongly inhibits CYP2C19 hepatic enzyme required for bioactivation of Clopidogrel into its active antiplatelet thiol metabolite.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Significantly attenuated platelet inhibition, leading to elevated risk of stent thrombosis, recurrent myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Switch Omeprazole to Pantoprazole (Pan 40) or Rabeprazole, which exhibit negligible CYP2C19 inhibition, or use an H2-receptor antagonist like Famotidine.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Synergistic enhancement of cyclic GMP-mediated vascular smooth muscle relaxation and systemic vasodilation.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Profound, refractory, life-threatening hypotension, syncope, myocardial ischemia, and cardiogenic shock.
drug_interactions.recommendation: STRICTLY CONTRAINDICATED. Never co-prescribe Sildenafil with sublingual or oral nitrates (Sorbitrate / Nitroglycerin).

drug_interactions.mechanism: Dual renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system (RAAS) blockade combining an ARB and an ACE inhibitor.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Significantly increased risk of acute kidney injury, severe hyperkalemia, and symptomatic hypotension without added cardiovascular benefit (ONTARGET trial).
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid dual RAAS blockade. Discontinue one agent and titrate monotherapy or add a complementary antihypertensive class (e.g. CCB like Amlodipine).

drug_interactions.mechanism: Ibuprofen binds competitively and reversibly to platelet COX-1 catalytic channels, sterically blocking irreversible acetylation by Aspirin.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Abolishes the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of low-dose Aspirin, leaving the patient unprotected against coronary thrombosis; also causes synergistic gastroduodenal ulceration and bleeding.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid regular concurrent use. If both are necessary, take immediate-release Aspirin at least 2 hours before or 8 hours after Ibuprofen, or substitute Paracetamol.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Dual non-steroidal anti-inflammatory and antiplatelet synergy causing profound gastroduodenal mucosal damage and systemic platelet inhibition.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Multi-fold increase in catastrophic upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage, peptic ulcer perforation, and blunted renal hemodynamics.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid concurrent NSAID with antiplatelet therapy whenever possible. Add prophylactic high-dose PPI (Pantoprazole 40mg).

drug_interactions.mechanism: Concomitant NSAID and Salicylate therapy multiplying gastrointestinal erosive injury and antiplatelet bleeding diathesis.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Severe gastric hemorrhage, prolonged bleeding time, and acute prerenal azotemia.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Do not co-prescribe. Use topical analgesics or non-NSAID options (e.g., Paracetamol monotherapy up to safe ceiling) for pain management.

drug_interactions.mechanism: NSAID-induced gastrointestinal erosion and inhibition of platelet aggregation combined with oral vitamin K antagonist anticoagulation.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: High-velocity internal and GI bleeding, hematemesis, intracranial hemorrhage risk.
drug_interactions.recommendation: CONTRAINDICATED in routine outpatient care. Use Paracetamol for mild-to-moderate analgesia and closely monitor INR.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Potentiation of anticoagulant hypoprothrombinemic effect and gastric mucosal compromise.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Massive gastrointestinal bleeding and elevated PT/INR.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination. If indispensable, intensive INR monitoring and PPI coverage are mandatory.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Part of the 'Triple Whammy' nephrotoxic triad: ARB dilates efferent arteriole while NSAID constricts afferent arteriole, drastically reducing glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Acute Kidney Injury (AKI), hyperkalemia, and blunting of Telmisartan antihypertensive efficacy.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid NSAID in patients on Telmisartan, particularly in elderly or dehydrated individuals. Monitor serum creatinine and potassium within 1-2 weeks.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Prostaglandin synthesis inhibition by Aceclofenac counteracts ARB renal hemodynamics and natriuresis.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Acute decline in renal function, fluid retention, worsening hypertension, hyperkalemia.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Limit duration to < 3-5 days; ensure adequate hydration and check renal markers.

drug_interactions.mechanism: NSAID inhibits vasodilatory prostaglandins, impairing renal autoregulation preserved by ACE inhibition.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Precipitation of acute renal failure and loss of blood pressure control.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid chronic NSAIDs with ACE inhibitors. Consider acetaminophen or topical agents.

drug_interactions.mechanism: NSAIDs inhibit intrarenal prostaglandin synthesis, reducing renal blood flow and antagonizing the natriuretic and diuretic efficacy of thiazides.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Reduced blood pressure control and elevated risk of acute renal dysfunction.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Monitor blood pressure and renal function. Minimize NSAID duration.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Polyvalent metal cation chelation: Calcium ions bind to Ciprofloxacin in the GI tract to form an insoluble, unabsorbable chelate complex.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Reduces Ciprofloxacin oral bioavailability by up to 50-70%, risking therapeutic failure and antimicrobial resistance development.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Space administration: Administer Ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after Calcium Carbonate (Shelcal) or antacids.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Divalent cation chelation markedly retarding GI absorption of Ofloxacin.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Subtherapeutic antibiotic concentrations leading to bacterial treatment failure.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Separate intake by at least 2 hours before or 4-6 hours after the calcium formulation.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Additive cardiac potassium hERG channel blockade prolonging ventricular repolarization (QT interval).
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Increased risk of QT interval prolongation, cardiac arrhythmia, and Torsades de Pointes.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Caution in patients with cardiac disease, electrolyte abnormalities, or elderly. Monitor ECG if combination cannot be avoided.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Additive cardiac QT prolongation risk from dual HERG-channel active medications.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Ventricular arrhythmias and syncope, especially in patients with hypokalemia or baseline long QT.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Avoid combination when feasible; consider alternative antiemetic (e.g., Ondansetron with monitoring or Metoclopramide) or monitor baseline ECG.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Fluoroquinolones augment pancreatic insulin release and displace sulfonylureas from plasma protein binding.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Severe, unpredictable, and refractory hypoglycemia.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Educate patient on hypoglycemia symptoms; increase blood glucose self-monitoring frequency while on Ciprofloxacin.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Azithromycin weakly inhibits CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein, increasing serum concentrations of Atorvastatin.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Heightened risk of statin-induced myopathy, myalgia, and rhabdomyolysis.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Temporarily withhold Atorvastatin during short-course Azithromycin therapy or advise patient to promptly report unexplained muscle pain/dark urine.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Potential additive QT interval prolongation and central nervous system depressant interactions.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Elevated risk of cardiac arrhythmias and prolonged sedation.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Use lowest effective doses and monitor clinical response.

drug_interactions.mechanism: PPI suppression of gastric acid reduces solubilization and ionization of insoluble Calcium Carbonate.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Modest reduction in calcium bioavailability; long-term PPI therapy with low calcium absorption is linked to bone mineral density decline.
drug_interactions.recommendation: Take Calcium Carbonate with meals to facilitate acid-independent absorption, or consider Calcium Citrate.

drug_interactions.mechanism: Long-term PPI use combined with Metformin can potentiate Vitamin B12 malabsorption.
drug_interactions.clinical_consequence: Gradual development of macrocytic anemia or peripheral neuropathy over prolonged therapy (>1-2 years).
drug_interactions.recommendation: Screen serum Vitamin B12 levels periodically in patients on long-term combined therapy.

sample_prescriptions.title: Hidden Combination Overdose (Fever & Back Pain)
sample_prescriptions.prescription_text:
Rx:
1. Tab Dolo 650 1 tab TDS
2. Tab Combiflam 1 tab BD
3. Tab Zerodol-P 1 tab BD SOS
4. Tab Pan 40 1 tab OD (BBF)
sample_prescriptions.clinical_trap: Combiflam contains Ibuprofen + Paracetamol (325mg). Zerodol-P contains Aceclofenac + Paracetamol (325mg). Along with Dolo 650 (650mg TDS = 1950mg), the cumulative daily Paracetamol hits 3,250mg - 3,900mg+, approaching the maximum hepatotoxic ceiling. Furthermore, concurrent Aceclofenac + Ibuprofen produces dual NSAID toxicity with high gastric ulcer and bleeding risk.

sample_prescriptions.title: The Elderly Diabetic 'Triple Whammy' AKI
sample_prescriptions.prescription_text:
Rx:
1. Tab Glycomet-GP 2 1 tab BD
2. Tab Telma-H 1 tab OD
3. Tab Combiflam 1 tab BD
4. Tab Pantocid 40 1 tab OD
sample_prescriptions.clinical_trap: Patient has severe renal impairment (eGFR 26). Glycomet-GP contains Metformin 500mg, which is CONTRAINDICATED at eGFR < 30 due to fatal lactic acidosis risk. Telma-H (Telmisartan + HCTZ) + Combiflam (Ibuprofen) creates the infamous 'Triple Whammy' (Diuretic + ARB + NSAID), shutting down renal autoregulation and inducing Acute Kidney Injury (AKI).

sample_prescriptions.title: Cardio-GI Danger & CYP2C19 Neutralization
sample_prescriptions.prescription_text:
Rx:
1. Tab Clopilet 75 1 tab OD
2. Tab Ecosprin 75 1 tab OD
3. Tab Omez 20 1 tab OD
4. Tab Voveran SR 100 1 tab OD SOS
5. Tab Atorva 20 1 tab HS
sample_prescriptions.clinical_trap: Omeprazole (Omez) is a potent CYP2C19 inhibitor that prevents bioactivation of Clopidogrel (Clopilet), nullifying its antiplatelet protection after stent placement! Additionally, adding Diclofenac (Voveran) on top of dual antiplatelet therapy (Aspirin + Clopidogrel) skyrockets the risk of massive upper GI bleeding.

sample_prescriptions.title: Pediatric Upper Respiratory & Chelation Trap
sample_prescriptions.prescription_text:
Rx:
1. Tab Cifran 500 1 tab BD
2. Tab Shelcal 500 1 tab OD
3. Tab Montair-LC 1 tab HS
4. Tab Calpol 500 1 tab TDS
sample_prescriptions.clinical_trap: Ciprofloxacin (Cifran) is swallowed concurrently with Calcium (Shelcal 500), forming an unabsorbable chelate complex that cuts antibiotic efficacy in half. Additionally, Ciprofloxacin is generally cautioned in children due to arthropathy/cartilage toxicity, and adult tablet Cifran 500 BD (1000mg/day) is an excessive dose for a 24kg child.
